<SUMMARY>The United States, under President Donald Trump, implemented significant export controls on advanced Artificial Intelligence models from Anthropic, restricting access for foreign nationals globally and raising concerns about AI nationalism. Concurrently, geopolitical dynamics in West Asia saw a potential de-escalation with President Trump signaling progress toward a US-Iran truce, leading to shifts in global commodity markets, alongside a historic direct meeting between Iran and the UAE. Critical mineral supply chains faced heightened scrutiny as China imposed export restrictions on indium phosphide and tungsten, impacting global tech and AI chip industries, while the Democratic Republic of Congo banned cobalt exports. These developments underscore a trend of increasing national-level control over strategic technologies and resources, driving calls for self-reliance in nations like India.</SUMMARY>

<EWS>The imposition of US export controls on advanced AI models may trigger stricter global regulations and increased investment risks across AI sectors, potentially accelerating AI nationalism among nations seeking technological sovereignty. China's new export restrictions on indium phosphide and tungsten highlight vulnerabilities in global AI chip and tech supply chains, signaling potential future disruptions and price volatility for key components. The reported progress toward a US-Iran truce, while de-escalatory, could rapidly alter energy markets and regional power balances, particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with implications for global oil flows and pricing. The Democratic Republic of Congo's cobalt export ban poses a direct threat to the global electric vehicle battery supply, indicating future price increases and diversification pressures for manufacturers.</EWS>

<EXEC>

**Asia:**
The EU Commission weaponized the Digital Services Act against the Chinese online platform Temu on June 13. Luxel Corporation appointed KOS, Inc. as its exclusive distributor in South Korea on June 12 for ultrathin freestanding polymer and metallized optical bandpass filters. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang outlined AI's shift from retrieval to generation on June 12. Economic security has been highlighted as national security on June 12. Japan aimed to beef up energy security cooperation with the Prime Minister's Europe tour on June 12 amid the Middle East conflict. The Nikkei Stock Average closed above the 66,000 level for the first time in a week on June 12 due to easing concerns over tensions in the Middle East and a strong rally in U.S. technology shares.

**Americas:**
The Trump administration imposed export restrictions on Anthropic AI systems on June 13. The US government ordered Anthropic to suspend access to its most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models, Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for all foreign nationals on June 13, citing national security authorities. Anthropic stated it would "abruptly disable" these models for all users on June 13, including foreign national Anthropic employees, after receiving the export control directive on June 12. Anthropic disputed the security concerns associated with Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on June 13.

**Europe:**
The US government directive on June 13 to suspend access to Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models for any foreign national applied globally. French foundation model developer Mistral AI SAS is reportedly in talks to raise €3 billion, or about $3.5 billion, from investors on June 13, which could value the company at €20 billion ($23.1 billion). The Prime Minister of the UK vowed to unleash AI tutors on 450,000 children on June 12. The UK set out an AI infrastructure push at London Tech Week on June 13.

**Oceania:**
A new report found on June 13 that Australia can capitalize on AI and has valuable cards to play strategically. Sharon AI, an Australian neocloud company listed on Nasdaq, surged about 25% on June 12 after announcing a six-year strategic compute collaboration with Nvidia. The agreement between Sharon AI and Nvidia involves enabling 72 megawatts of new data center capacity on June 12.

</EXEC>

<LITHO>

**Asia:**
SK Hynix stated on June 12 that it plans to boost memory production threefold. Pingtung broke ground on Taiwan's first semiconductor supply chain park on June 12.

**Americas:**
Bechtel is set to build a $100 billion semiconductor plant, which will be the biggest in the US, according to a June 12 report. Forge Nano secured a semiconductor wafer fab equipment order on June 11. Bangladesh secured semiconductor partnerships with Intel, Synopsys, and SanDisk during a US roadshow on June 13. The 3D Semiconductor Packaging Market CAGR is projected to be at 14.8% from 2026 to 2030, reaching $36.05 billion in industry revenue by 2030, according to a June 12 report.

</LITHO>

<REE>

**Africa:**
Orion Critical Mineral Consortium (Orion CMC), backed by the US and Abu Dhabi, is evaluating the acquisition of a stake in the French mining operator Eramet, which is partly owned by the French Government, according to a June 12 report. The Democratic Republic of Congo’s cobalt export ban on June 11 spells trouble for the world and puts EV battery supply at risk.

**Americas:**
The U.S. Government took a 10% stake in a mining company on June 12. Antimony, used in ammunition, flame retardants, and next-generation batteries, is becoming a national-security priority, with the United States producing almost none of it, according to a June 12 report. Mining activities in the Boundary Waters wilderness of northeastern Minnesota risk impacting a pristine area, as highlighted on June 12.

**Asia:**
AXT Inc. rose 10% on June 12 as Chinese export restrictions squeezed the global indium phosphide supply. China’s export curbs on tungsten on June 13 threaten Japan’s AI chip supply chain.

**Europe:**
Metso invested in new mineralogy analysis equipment in Finland on June 12, installing a TESCAN TIMA automated mineralogy analyser at its research facility.

</REE>

**Europe:**
Hanne Nabintu Herland stated on June 12 that economic security is national security. Europe’s race to secure power for data centers and electrification projects is intense, with customers paying to secure spots in production queues for gas turbines, according to Siemens Energy AG on June 12.

Antimony is highlighted as a national-security priority on June 12 due to its use in ammunition.

Missile defense worked against Iran but might not work against China, according to a June 12 analysis.

</MILITARY>

<CONCLUSION>The imposition of US export controls on Anthropic's advanced AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for foreign nationals marks a significant escalation in AI nationalism, affecting global market dynamics and spurring calls for AI self-reliance in countries like India. China's new export restrictions on critical minerals like indium phosphide and tungsten have immediately impacted global tech supply chains, underscoring the fragility of these networks and driving efforts for diversification. In West Asia, the week was characterized by complex diplomatic shifts, including President Trump signaling progress toward a US-Iran truce, a historic face-to-face meeting between the UAE and Iran, and an Israeli cyber firm facing accusations of election interference across multiple continents. These developments collectively highlight an increasingly fragmented global landscape where technological leadership, resource control, and regional stability are actively contested and recalibrated.</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>DLI-backed chip companies urged the Indian government for stronger market access and intellectual property protection, highlighting the need for procurement support to foster growth and maintain domestic ownership on June 13. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal stated on June 12 that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 12-year tenure transformed the Northeast into a national priority and accelerated Assam’s growth. The US directive suspending access to Anthropic's AI models spurred India Inc's push for self-reliance in AI infrastructure, with technology leaders calling for domestic R&D, open-source models, and semiconductor design to ensure national sovereignty on June 13. Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu stressed the need for India to develop its own technologies and adopt smaller, Indian-developed, and open-source AI models on June 13, following the US restrictions on advanced AI models. Indian companies are rapidly investing in electric trucks, driven by fluctuating diesel prices and a focus on sustainability, with major firms like Ultratech Cement and Vedanta expanding their electric fleets, as reported on June 12. Naga groups opposed a new energy exploration deal between the Centre, Assam, and Nagaland on June 12, arguing that natural resource ownership is part of the agreed political settlement. India is set to decide on extending customs duty relief for critical raw material imports beyond June 30, with an inter-ministerial panel reviewing easing import curbs and considering fresh duties on certain locally manufactured electronics, as reported on June 12. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma proposed a new development approach called 'Geographic Equity' at a NITI meet on June 12 to ensure growth benefits reach all regions of India. Nvidia's market cap reached $4.9 trillion on June 12, becoming worth more than India’s entire stock market. The FSSAI issued a strict directive on June 12 to all food business operators to immediately cease using metallic pins and wires for packaging food items and parcels. The Industry is working with the government on the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, focusing on supply chain, talent, and IP, according to IESA on June 11.</INDIA>

<WEST_ASIA>Israeli cyber firm BlackCore was accused on June 13 by French disinformation agency Viginum of interfering in municipal elections in France, New York City, Scotland, Angola, and Togo, allegedly targeting pro-Palestinian political candidates. A U.S. precision airstrike struck a water facility in Iran that provides potable water to civilians on June 13, raising legal questions. The Strait of Hormuz is effectively under Iranian control, with oil tankers forced to pay tolls in Chinese yuan instead of U.S. dollars, according to a June 13 book. Gold prices surged 3.4% to $4,212.26 an ounce on June 13, following President Donald Trump’s statement signaling progress toward a US-Iran truce. Iran and the UAE held their first historic direct meeting since the U.S.-Israel-Iran war erupted in October 2023 on June 13, signaling a potential recalibration in Gulf politics. Oil prices dropped to nearly two-month lows on June 13 amid reports of an imminent US-Iran peace deal. Global equities rose on June 13, and oil prices slid on Gulf peace hopes. Turkey's President Erdogan intensified his rhetoric against Israel on June 13, which Israeli officials described as "unbearable," citing interests in Syria and viewing the Israel-Greece-Cyprus partnership in the Mediterranean as a "strategic problem" for Turkey. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman canceled an Abu Dhabi trip on June 12 amid tensions. Avtandil Kalandadze, master of a ghost fleet tanker that transported Iran- and Venezuela-origin oil, pleaded guilty on June 12 in U.S. District Court for refusing to obey orders from the U.S. Coast Guard during a weeks-long pursuit. Armenia’s Western pivot survived Moscow’s pressure campaign on June 12, with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan winning re-election and keeping the country on a Western trajectory. The UAE's oil giant stated on June 14 that full Hormuz flows are not expected until the first half of 2027. The US, Greece, Cyprus, and Israel launched the East Med Energy Center in Houston on June 12. The UAE emerged as one of the world's most receptive markets for AI-powered shopping on June 14. An AI-generated film showing violence in Iran was reported on June 13 by The New York Times.</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming weeks are likely to see continued friction over AI technology access and critical mineral supply chains, potentially leading to further nationalistic policies and protective measures by major global powers. The US export controls on advanced AI models could precipitate a global restructuring of AI development and deployment, with nations accelerating efforts toward domestic AI infrastructure and open-source alternatives. West Asia's geopolitical landscape remains highly fluid, with the potential US-Iran truce talks and regional diplomatic shifts suggesting a volatile yet possibly de-escalatory trend, which will significantly influence global energy markets. The strategic competition for technological and resource dominance is poised to intensify, demanding adaptive strategies from governments and industries navigating these complex interdependencies.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
